patch.value:
Source: https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1456

## Problem
`pm update many` exists, but there is no CLI counterpart for creating items in bulk. An agent that needs to record N items has to spawn N `pm create` processes, and each one pays full startup plus workspace load. Typical cases:
- importing findings or review threads;
- mirroring notes into the tracker;
- seeding a plan;
- converting a spec into tasks.

**Measured on 2026.10.13** (Linux, Node 26, a tracker of about 940 items growing to about 1,200):
- 266 sequential `pm --json create --type <custom type> --title … --description … --body-file … --tags …` calls took **10 m 24 s wall time**, about 2.3 s per item.
- 2 m 54 s of that was user CPU, so most of the cost is per-process startup and workspace reads, repeated 266 times.
- The run is not atomic. An interruption leaves a partial import, and the caller has to build its own idempotency, for example by listing existing items and matching on a custom key field.

The SDK already has the primitive. #613 added a bulk multi-item atomic-mutation helper on top of `commitWorkspaceTransaction`. It just isn't reachable from the CLI.

## Proposal
`pm create many` (alias `pm create --from -`) reads JSONL or a JSON array from a file or stdin. Each record uses the same field names as `pm create` flags or their JSON equivalents, including custom fields, `body`, `tags`, dependencies and comments.
- One process and one workspace transaction: all records are created or none, with history and merge receipts written as usual.
- `--dry-run` validates every record first: types, required custom fields, dependency references (including references to other records in the same batch, through client-side `ref` keys), and duplicate-title detection against the existing tracker.
- Optional idempotency key, `--upsert-by <field>`: an existing item whose field matches is updated instead of duplicated. That makes re-running an import safe.
- The `--json` receipt lists created and updated ids in input order, mapped to each record's `ref`.

## Why it matters for agents
Project management is context management. The moments an agent wants to write many items at once (triage imports, review-thread capture, plan expansion) are exactly the moments a 2-3 s per-item cost and a non-atomic loop push it to skip tracking or to batch lossy summaries instead.

value.text:
Implementation note (2026-10-15): bulk creation lands on the existing atomic surface instead of a new top-level command. The SDK resolver now accepts JSON Lines, single records, and op-less create documents (pm create field names, optionally wrapped as {ref, item}); records without ref/id receive row-<n> aliases; declared schema fields are admitted on create/update option rows via their option targets. A new planner, planItemMutationDocument, reads the workspace (schema hydration also under the configuration-only dry-run scope, where declared fields otherwise vanish), derives a stable transaction id from the document bytes when none is given, and resolves --upsert-key against existing items (custom or core field): one match becomes an update (rows[].upserted), a missing key, an in-batch duplicate, or several matches refuse before any write. CLI adds --from <path> and --upsert-key and makes --transaction-id optional; MCP pm_mutate accepts item rows, upsertKey and an optional transactionId. pm create many refuses with bulk_create_route and names the route. The journal/plan mismatch is now a typed transaction_plan_mismatch refusal instead of an unknown_error.

Measured in a sandbox: 2-record JSON Lines import committed in one transaction; replay returned recovered:true with no duplicates; upsert by external_id updated the matched item and created the unmatched one; dry-run under the configuration-only scope validated with the declared field present.

value.text: Review follow-up (PR #1479, CodeRabbit full review, 2026-10-15): (1) keyed upsert no longer matches the ids this document itself would create (deterministic ids from the transaction id, plus explicit create ids), so a committed import re-run with --upsert-key and a derived transaction id keeps its original create plan and the journal recovers it (recovered:true) instead of refusing with transaction_plan_mismatch; integration test added. (2) options-based create rows that become updates keep their declared runtime-field option keys (externalId) instead of dropping them. Both covered by unit tests. Hosted CI also required escape_class and structured gate_evidence on the closed Issues of this change (defect-evidence gate), now recorded.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Review follow-up (PR #1479, CodeRabbit): the docs/SDK.md planItemMutationDocument upsert example gave the second row no external_id, so the documented upsert_key_missing refusal would have stopped it; the row now carries ext-2 so the example runs as written.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Review follow-up (PR #1479, CodeRabbit, third pass): keyed upsert converted a matched create row to an update and deleted its ref before reference collection, so a later row addressing it as @ref failed with Unknown mutation reference and the rows receipt omitted that ref. The matched alias is now recorded against the existing id before conversion, and the receipt reads aliases from the input rows, so upserted rows keep their ref and later rows resolve @ref to the matched item.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Review follow-up (PR #1479, CodeRabbit, fourth pass): the suggested unconditional exact-title refusal in planItemMutationDocument was not adopted. Every create row already runs the full SDK create path in both the staged dry-run and the commit, so governance.duplicate_detection_mode (strict refuses, advisory warns, off opts out, --allow-duplicate honoured) applies per row exactly as for pm create. The dry-run receipt does, however, discard the per-row advisory warnings; that gap is owned by pm-ekf2gu.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Review follow-up (PR #1479, CodeRabbit, fifth pass): stableUpsertValue serialized non-string key values with JSON.stringify, so two equivalent object values with different key insertion order never matched and the row stayed a create. Plain-object keys are now sorted recursively before serialization (arrays keep their order), and the unit spec covers an object-valued upsert key matching on content.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Review follow-up (PR #1479, CodeRabbit, sixth pass): keyed upsert was resolved before the writer lock and never re-checked, so two concurrent plans with different transaction ids could each create an item for the same key value. Create rows that matched nothing now carry a unique {key,value} guard; commitItemMutations and previewItemMutations re-check it under the lock through a per-transaction lazily scanned index (own create ids excluded so replays stay recovered) and refuse with upsert_key_conflict before any write. A re-run re-plans the row as an update. Schema and candidate helpers moved from the planner into item-transaction (resolveTransactionSchema, listUpsertKeyCandidates); MCP pm_mutate rows admit unique; docs/COMMANDS.md and docs/SDK.md describe the guard; unit and integration tests cover the race, the preview, the replay, and malformed guards.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Review follow-up (PR #1479, CodeRabbit, eighth pass): canonicalizeUpsertValue sorted object keys with localeCompare, which can report distinct keys (precomposed and decomposed e-acute) as equal, so insertion order could leak into the canonical JSON and the planner or the lock-held guard could miss an existing key. Keys now sort by code units; the unit spec covers collating-equal keys in different orders.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Review follow-up (PR #1479, CodeRabbit, ninth pass): a keyed-upsert row that matched before the writer lock became a plain update by id, so a concurrent writer could change or remove the key after planning and the update would still land. Converted rows now carry match {key,value}; the update step re-reads the key under the lock and refuses with upsert_match_changed (CONFLICT) before writing. Verifying the re-run path exposed a second gap: a compensated attempt under a derived transaction id refused the re-planned document with transaction_plan_mismatch because the journal still demanded the old step ids. parseJournal now treats a compensated journal as holding nothing to resume, so the re-plan starts attempt 2 under the same id while applying, compensating, and committed journals still replay only their own plan. Unit tests cover the journal rule and the guard shapes; the integration race test covers the moved key, the preview, and the re-plan commit.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Review follow-up (PR #1479, CodeRabbit, tenth pass): three more planner gaps closed. An explicit ref equal to the row-<n> alias a later row would be synthesized surfaced only as a misleading 'Duplicate mutation ref'; synthesis now refuses up front naming the colliding row and the reserved prefix. An options row carrying a declared field whose metadata_key differs from its option name (key classification, metadata_key escape_class) was reported as upsert_key_missing because readUpsertKeyValue only tried the metadata key and its camelCase form; it now resolves the declared option target first. The MCP pm_mutate commit phase built its extension scope from the raw path while plan and preview used the resolved root; all three phases now share one scope.
